logic_errors.issue: Cancellation detection treats a legitimate downstream write-half-close as a disconnected client.
logic_errors.scenario: A client sends a complete authenticated HTTP request, calls shutdown(SHUT_WR), and continues reading its response. recv(MSG_PEEK) returns zero because the client has finished sending, not because it cannot receive. The progress callback cancels the upstream request.
logic_errors.evidence: Reproduced against a fresh container build using the existing synthetic router fixture: the complete valid request returned HTTP 502 and the upstream sink received zero requests.
logic_errors.recommendation: Do not use receive-side EOF alone as proof that the downstream cannot receive a response. Preserve valid half-closed connections while retaining bounded cancellation of genuinely disconnected clients.
logic_errors.recommended_regression: Send a complete Content-Length request over a raw socket, call shutdown(SHUT_WR), and assert HTTP 200, an intact response body, and exactly one upstream request. Retain the existing idle-stream cancellation regression.

logic_errors.issue: The models endpoint can terminate the gateway on an allocation failure.
logic_errors.scenario: If json_dumps returns NULL under memory pressure, the /v1/models handler passes NULL to reply(), which immediately calls strlen(NULL). The earlier json_pack and array-append failures are also unchecked, allowing failed construction to reach this path.
logic_errors.evidence: Static inspection of the current handler and reply helper; allocation-failure injection was not performed.
logic_errors.recommendation: Check JSON construction, append, and serialization results; release partial objects and return a generic failure without passing NULL to reply().
logic_errors.recommended_regression: Inject failures into JSON allocation/construction and serialization while requesting authenticated /v1/models. Assert no crash, no partial success response, and continued service after the injected failure.

suggestions.suggestion: Add deterministic allocation-failure tests for PCRE2 general-context, match-data, match-context, and match-time allocations. The current code appears to fail closed, and the existing match-limit regression passes, but allocation-failure behavior is not exercised by the reviewed integration suite.

Single-instance operation, static policies, lack of universal PII recognition, and absence of pooling or UI were treated as initial-release limitations, not defects. No concrete public-egress bypass or private-failure fallback was established in this review.

summary: Reviewed the requested diff and current production files, including untracked compliance implementation and tests. Fresh builds in recursant-v4-dev:local passed all six CTest groups. An additional synthetic regression reproduced incorrect cancellation of a valid half-closed client; static inspection also found an unchecked allocation-failure crash in /v1/models. Router changes arriving during integration were reread, and final file hashes remained stable across subsequent checks. No repository files, credentials, services, or configuration were modified; only disposable container-local build/test artifacts were created. Containers used a read-only source mount and disabled external networking; no live model calls or prohibited secret-file reads were performed.
